project.name: identity-aware-agent
project.description: A secure, multi-tier AI agent system where user identity propagates from frontend authentication through an A2A gateway and Google ADK agent down to resource APIs. Access control is enforced at three independent levels (agent, tool, and resource) using Cedar RBAC/ABAC policies, providing defense in depth across Microsoft Entra ID and AWS Cognito identity providers.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: A2A protocol gateway (FastAPI) that validates multi-IdP JWTs, enforces agent-level group ACLs, propagates identity via ContextVars, and exposes the /me security-context endpoint backed by a Cedar PDP.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ContextVars for async-safe per-request auth propagation and an IdPConfig dataclass to route JWT validation across Entra and Cognito issuers.

nodes.name: IdPConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a single identity provider's JWKS URIs, valid issuers/audiences, signing algorithms, and audience-claim name used during token validation.

nodes.name: TokenValidator
nodes.summary: Multi-IdP JWT validator that detects the provider from the iss claim, fetches and caches JWKS keys, and verifies signature/issuer/audience for Entra and Cognito tokens.
nodes.languageNotes: JWKS cache auto-clears on a key-not-found miss and re-fetches; handles Cognito's non-standard client_id audience claim.

nodes.name: IdentityAwareAgentExecutor
nodes.summary: A2A AgentExecutor that bridges incoming tasks to the downstream ADK agent, ensuring a per-user session exists and forwarding identity, role, and ABAC attributes on each chat call.

nodes.name: auth_middleware
nodes.summary: ASGI middleware that extracts the Bearer token, validates it, enforces blocklist and group-membership checks, and stores claims/token/role/ABAC attributes in ContextVars for the request.

nodes.name: get_me
nodes.summary: Handler for the GET /me endpoint that returns the caller's security context (roles, groups, scopes, expiry) and batch-evaluates per-tool permissions via the Cedar evaluator.

nodes.name: _build_idp_configs
nodes.summary: Builds the list of IdPConfig objects for Entra and Cognito from environment variables, defining their JWKS endpoints and validation parameters.

nodes.name: _extract_user_info
nodes.summary: Normalizes provider-specific JWT claims (Entra vs Cognito) into a common user-info dict with id, email, name, and department.

nodes.name: _make_task_event
nodes.summary: Constructs an A2A TaskStatusUpdateEvent carrying a text message and final flag for streaming task progress back to the client.

nodes.name: _auth_error
nodes.summary: Builds a standardized JSON auth-error Response with CORS headers and a denial_reason field for the frontend's denial classifier.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: Google ADK agent service (FastAPI) that manages per-user sessions, injects identity headers into MCP tool calls, and runs buffered/streaming chat against Claude Haiku via LiteLLM with rate-limit retry.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an McpToolset header provider to inject Authorization, X-Assume-Role, and X-Abac-Attrs from ADK session state on every MCP request.

nodes.name: IdentityAwareAgent
nodes.summary: Wraps a Google ADK LlmAgent with identity-aware session management, role determination, and a retrying chat loop that calls MCP tools with the user's propagated auth context.
nodes.languageNotes: Rate-limit retry uses 3 attempts with 30s/60s/90s backoff; RunConfig caps LLM calls at 4 to prevent loops.

nodes.name: mcp_header_provider
nodes.summary: Sync header provider invoked by McpToolset that injects Authorization, X-Assume-Role, and X-Abac-Attrs headers from the ADK session state into each MCP request.

nodes.name: create_session
nodes.summary: POST /session route handler that extracts the Bearer token, validates the user id against token claims, and creates a new identity-bound ADK session.

nodes.name: _parse_chat_request
nodes.summary: Shared helper that extracts and validates the Bearer token and chat-request body fields for the /chat and /chat/stream endpoints.

nodes.name: chat
nodes.summary: POST /chat handler that primes session state with role/ABAC attributes and returns the agent's buffered text response.

nodes.name: chat_stream
nodes.summary: POST /chat/stream handler that returns the agent's response as an SSE StreamingResponse.

nodes.name: _validate_user_id
nodes.summary: Decodes the access token (without signature verification) to confirm the supplied user_id matches the token's subject claim.

nodes.name: dev_config.py
nodes.summary: Shared development configuration module that loads dev_config.toml, exposes the auth-bypass flag per server, parses ABAC attribute headers, detects the IdP from claims, and holds shared path constants.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tomllib to read an optional gitignored dev_config.toml; warns once per section when auth bypass is enabled.

nodes.name: is_auth_disabled
nodes.summary: Returns whether auth bypass is enabled for a given server section in dev_config.toml, logging a one-time warning when active.

nodes.name: parse_abac_attrs
nodes.summary: Parses the JSON-encoded X-Abac-Attrs header into a dict while filtering out blocked ABAC keys that must come from validated claims.

nodes.name: detect_provider
nodes.summary: Detects the identity provider (entra vs cognito) by inspecting the iss claim of the decoded token.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: FastMCP tool server exposing 18 tools (Graph, S3, time, ServiceNow) guarded by a two-phase Cedar authorization model via require_cedar and UserContextMiddleware, with OBO token exchange for Graph and ServiceNow.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs in stateless HTTP mode using ContextVars (6 vars) instead of session state; Phase 1 RBAC passthrough lets ABAC tools defer to Phase 2 context checks.

nodes.name: UserContextMiddleware
nodes.summary: FastMCP middleware that resolves user identity from the validated token (or bypass), sets the six auth ContextVars, and enforces role selection on list-tools and call-tool hooks.

nodes.name: require_cedar
nodes.summary: Factory returning a FastMCP auth callable that performs the Phase 1 Cedar RBAC check for a named tool, with passthrough for ABAC tools that need runtime context.

nodes.name: cedar_check_with_context
nodes.summary: Performs the Phase 2 Cedar ABAC check inside a tool, evaluating the policy with runtime context such as the S3 resource path.

nodes.name: _cedar_check_department
nodes.summary: Composite role+department Cedar pre-check for ServiceNow tools, comparing the caller's JWT department claim against the target department before the SN call.

nodes.name: _build_auth
nodes.summary: Builds the FastMCP MultiAuth verifier chain combining an Azure JWT verifier for Entra and a JWT verifier for Cognito.

nodes.name: _get_effective_graph_token
nodes.summary: Returns a (token, obo_used) tuple, exchanging the user's token for a Graph-scoped OBO token when available or falling back to the raw token.

nodes.name: _get_effective_sn_token
nodes.summary: Returns a (token, obo_used) tuple for ServiceNow calls, performing OBO exchange for Entra users when configured and otherwise signalling service-account fallback.

nodes.name: _run_s3_operation
nodes.summary: Wraps boto3 S3 calls in asyncio.to_thread with standardized error mapping for the S3 tool family.

nodes.name: get_user_profile
nodes.summary: MCP tool that returns the user's profile from Microsoft Graph via OBO, falling back to token claims when OBO is unavailable.

nodes.name: list_files
nodes.summary: MCP tool that lists OneDrive files for the user via a Graph OBO token, returning an informative error when OBO is not configured.

nodes.name: delete_s3_object
nodes.summary: ABAC-protected MCP tool that deletes an S3 object only when the Phase 2 Cedar check passes (archiver=true and archive/* path), blocked in protected/.

nodes.name: list_s3_objects
nodes.summary: MCP tool that lists objects in an S3 bucket under an optional prefix using server-side AWS credentials.

nodes.name: get_s3_object_info
nodes.summary: MCP tool returning metadata for a single S3 object via server-side AWS credentials.

nodes.name: get_current_time
nodes.summary: MCP utility tool returning the current time in a requested timezone with resolution of common timezone aliases.

nodes.name: convert_timezone
nodes.summary: MCP utility tool that converts a time string from one timezone to another.

nodes.name: get_time_difference
nodes.summary: MCP utility tool that computes the UTC offset difference between two timezones.

nodes.name: list_articles
nodes.summary: ServiceNow MCP tool that lists knowledge-base articles after a composite role+department Cedar pre-check, using the OBO or service-account SN client.

nodes.name: list_incidents
nodes.summary: ServiceNow MCP tool that lists incidents for a department after a Cedar dept-scoped pre-check.

nodes.name: create_incident
nodes.summary: ServiceNow MCP tool that creates an incident in the caller's department after a dept-scoped Cedar pre-check.

nodes.name: update_incident
nodes.summary: ServiceNow MCP tool that updates an existing incident by sys_id after a dept-scoped Cedar pre-check.

nodes.name: list_knowledge_bases
nodes.summary: ServiceNow MCP tool that lists available knowledge bases for the user via the SN client.

nodes.name: policy.py
nodes.summary: Policy abstraction layer defining the PolicyEvaluator interface and its TOML and Cedar implementations, where CedarPolicyEvaluator composes TOML role resolution with cedarpy policy decisions and batch evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: CedarPolicyEvaluator hot-reloads policies and entities on mtime change and exposes check_access_batch for single-pass multi-tool evaluation.

nodes.name: CedarPolicyEvaluator
nodes.summary: Cedar-backed policy evaluator that loads policies/entities, builds the User entity from claims, and authorizes single and batch tool requests via cedarpy with mtime-based hot reload.

nodes.name: TomlPolicyEvaluator
nodes.summary: Policy evaluator that resolves group-to-role mappings from permissions.toml and answers role-availability and access queries from static TOML rules.

nodes.name: PolicyEvaluator
nodes.summary: Abstract base interface declaring get_available_roles and check_access for pluggable authorization backends.

nodes.name: AccessRequest
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing the principal, action, resource, and context of an authorization request.

nodes.name: AccessDecision
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing an authorization outcome (allowed flag plus reason).

nodes.name: graph_obo.py
nodes.summary: On-Behalf-Of token exchange for Microsoft Graph, providing the GraphOBOExchanger singleton that swaps a user's custom-audience token for a Graph-scoped token using the confidential client credential.
nodes.languageNotes: Caches per-scope credentials (LRU 128) and exposes module-level init/get accessors for the singleton.

nodes.name: GraphOBOExchanger
nodes.summary: Exchanges a user access token for a Graph-scoped OBO token using MSAL confidential-client credentials, caching credentials by scope.

nodes.name: servicenow.py
nodes.summary: ServiceNow Table API client supporting Bearer (OBO) or HTTP Basic (service account) auth, with methods for knowledge bases, articles, and incident CRUD plus a module-level singleton accessor.

nodes.name: ServiceNowClient
nodes.summary: HTTP client for the ServiceNow Table API exposing KB and incident operations, selecting Bearer OBO or service-account Basic auth per request.

nodes.name: init_servicenow_client
nodes.summary: Initializes the module-level ServiceNow client singleton from instance URL and service-account credentials.

nodes.name: servicenow_obo.py
nodes.summary: On-Behalf-Of token exchange for ServiceNow, providing the ServiceNowOBOExchanger singleton that swaps a user's token for a ServiceNow-scoped token so SN can apply per-user ACLs.
nodes.languageNotes: Dormant until [servicenow].obo_scope is configured; mirrors the GraphOBOExchanger init/get singleton pattern.

nodes.name: ServiceNowOBOExchanger
nodes.summary: Exchanges a user access token for a ServiceNow-scoped OBO token using MSAL confidential-client credentials, caching the credential.

nodes.name: servicenow_mock.py
nodes.summary: In-memory ServiceNow mock used when no instance URL is configured, mirroring the real client's KB and incident API surface with seeded data.

nodes.name: ServiceNowMockClient
nodes.summary: In-memory stand-in for ServiceNowClient that serves seeded knowledge bases, articles, and incidents for local development and testing.

nodes.name: rbac.cedar
nodes.summary: Cedar RBAC permit policies granting admin all tools (except ABAC-only delete_s3_object), developers a fixed tool set plus ServiceNow reads, and viewers a limited tool set; all authenticated users may list tools.
nodes.languageNotes: Role membership is modeled via the Cedar entity hierarchy (User in [Role]); delete_s3_object is intentionally excluded from all RBAC permits.

nodes.name: abac.cedar
nodes.summary: Cedar ABAC permit policies: archiver=true users may delete S3 objects in archive/* regardless of role, and developer/viewer may use dept-scoped ServiceNow tools only when their department claim matches the target department.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite role+department checks compare principal.department against context.target_department supplied at the agent layer.

nodes.name: guardrails.cedar
nodes.summary: Cedar forbid guardrail that blocks deletion of S3 objects under protected/* for everyone, overriding all permits including admin.
nodes.languageNotes: In Cedar a forbid always overrides any permit, making this a hard safety limit.

nodes.name: schema.cedarschema
nodes.summary: Cedar schema for the AgentAuth namespace defining the Role/User/Tool/S3Folder entities (with provider, email, groups, department, archiver attributes) and the call_tool and list_tools actions with their context.

nodes.name: entities.json
nodes.summary: Static Cedar entity store declaring the three roles (admin, developer, viewer) and 18 Tool entities with sensitivity and required-provider attributes used during policy evaluation.

nodes.summary: Python project configuration (uv) declaring project metadata and pytest options for the identity-aware agent backend.

nodes.name: permissions.example.toml

nodes.summary: MSAL configuration for Entra ID plus scope presets (loginRequest and per-tool graphScopes) used to drive consented token acquisition.

nodes.name: cognitoConfig.js

nodes.name: ConversationTabs.js

nodes.name: DenialIndicator.js

nodes.name: LoginPrompt.js
nodes.summary: Unauthenticated sign-in prompt offering provider selection (Entra or Cognito) via the useAuth login flow.

nodes.name: RBACTestMatrix.js

nodes.name: SecurityContextPanel.js

nodes.name: TokenInspector.js

nodes.name: a2aClient.js

nodes.name: constants.js
nodes.summary: Shared frontend constants holding the A2A server URL and provider display-label map.

nodes.name: denialClassifier.js
nodes.summary: Classifies an A2A response into one of four denial tiers (agent, tool, scope, resource) by inspecting HTTP status and response text patterns.

nodes.name: create_test_token

nodes.name: _user_entity

nodes.name: TestCedarABAC

nodes.name: TestCedarFilePolicies

nodes.name: TestCedarPolicyEvaluator

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what this project is: a secure, multi-tier AI agent system where a user's identity propagates from the browser all the way down to resource APIs, with access control enforced independently at three layers. The EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY frames the business value and the defense-in-depth security model. Read these first so the request path in the following steps has context.

tour.title: Frontend Boot & Multi-IdP Auth
tour.description: The React app boots from index.js, which mounts App.js wrapped in the unified AuthProvider. AuthProvider is the highest fan-in module in the codebase (9 dependents) because every component reads identity through its useAuth() hook. It hides two very different identity providers â€” MSAL for Entra ID and AWS Amplify for Cognito â€” behind one interface, so the rest of the UI never branches on provider. This is where the user's journey begins: a token is acquired here and carried through every later tier.
tour.languageLesson: React Context + a custom useAuth() hook is the idiomatic way to expose cross-cutting state (here, the authenticated session) without prop-drilling. AuthProvider returns the same shape regardless of whether MSAL or Amplify is active, an adapter pattern that keeps multi-IdP complexity out of the components.

tour.title: Frontend to Gateway Client
tour.description: Building on the token from Step 2, a2aClient.js is the single choke point through which the UI talks to the backend. It sends A2A JSON-RPC message/send requests with the Bearer token plus the X-Assume-Role and X-Abac-Attrs headers, then runs every response through denialClassifier.js. The classifier is the heart of the demo: it sorts failures into four tiers (agent, tool, scope, resource) so the dashboard can show exactly which security layer rejected a request.

tour.title: Tier 1 â€” A2A Gateway
tour.description: This is the BFS root and the first security tier. The A2A gateway (FastAPI) validates the incoming JWT against the correct IdP's JWKS, enforces agent-level group ACLs and a user blocklist, then propagates the identity downstream via ContextVars. It also serves the /me endpoint that the SecurityContextPanel in the UI reads to show role, groups, scopes and permissions. A request that fails here never reaches the agent â€” this is the 'agent' denial tier.
tour.languageLesson: Python's contextvars provide async-safe, per-request state without threading globals â€” each await chain sees its own copy. The gateway stashes the validated claims and access token in ContextVars so deeply nested async handlers can read identity without passing it through every function signature.

tour.title: The ADK Agent & Identity Header Injection
tour.description: Once the gateway admits a request, the Google ADK agent takes over: it manages a per-user session, runs the conversation against Claude Haiku via LiteLLM, and decides which tools to call. The pivotal piece is mcp_header_provider, which re-injects the user's Authorization, X-Assume-Role, and X-Abac-Attrs headers onto every outbound MCP tool call. This is how identity survives the hop from the agent into the tool tier rather than being lost at the LLM boundary.

tour.title: Tier 2 â€” MCP Tool Server
tour.description: The FastMCP server exposes all 18 identity-aware tools (Graph, S3, time, ServiceNow) and is the second security tier. Tied with policy.py for the highest backend fan-in, it is where the request finally meets a guardable action. Its UserContextMiddleware rebuilds the per-user ContextVars from the injected headers, and every @mcp.tool() is wrapped with require_cedar("tool_name") so no tool runs before authorization. A rejection here surfaces as the 'tool' denial tier in the UI.
tour.languageLesson: Because the MCP server runs in stateless HTTP mode (stateless_http=True), there is no server-side session to hang state on. The code uses ContextVars rebuilt per request by middleware instead of ctx.get_state(), keeping every tool call self-contained and horizontally scalable.

tour.title: The Cedar Authorization Engine
tour.description: policy.py is the brain behind Tier 2: CedarPolicyEvaluator composes TOML group-to-role resolution with cedarpy policy decisions and exposes batch evaluation for the /me endpoint. It loads the Cedar schema and the three policy files, evaluating them in a two-phase model â€” an RBAC pre-check (can this role call this tool at all?) followed by an ABAC runtime check (can this specific user do this specific operation?). This engine is consulted by both the MCP tier and the A2A gateway's /me endpoint.
tour.languageLesson: This is policy-as-data: authorization rules live in declarative Cedar files, not in Python if-statements. The PolicyEvaluator interface lets a TOML evaluator and a Cedar evaluator be swapped behind one contract, so the enforcement code never hard-codes a single policy engine.

tour.title: Cedar Policies, Schema & Entities
tour.description: Here are the actual authorization rules the engine from Step 7 evaluates. The schema declares the entity types (User, Role, Tool, S3Folder) and their attributes (provider, groups, department, archiver); entities.json supplies the three concrete roles and 18 tool definitions. The three policy files layer RBAC permits (role to tools), ABAC permits (archiver may delete in archive/, department-scoped ServiceNow access), and a forbid guardrail that blocks deletion under protected/ â€” a forbid that overrides even admin permits.
tour.languageLesson: Cedar evaluates all matching policies and applies a deny-overrides (forbid-wins) resolution: a single forbid beats any number of permits. This is why guardrails.cedar can block delete in protected/* for everyone, including admins, regardless of what the RBAC permits allow.

tour.title: Tier 3 â€” Resource Access & OBO Token Exchange
tour.description: After Cedar permits a tool, the deepest BFS layer reaches the actual resource APIs â€” and the third security tier. graph_obo.py performs an On-Behalf-Of exchange, swapping the user's custom-audience token for a Graph-scoped one so Microsoft Graph enforces its own OAuth scopes. The ServiceNow client mirrors this: with OBO enabled it sends the user's exchanged token so ServiceNow applies per-user ACLs; otherwise it falls back to a service account, and an in-memory mock stands in when no instance is configured. A failure here is the 'resource' denial tier.

tour.title: Shared Configuration
tour.description: Underpinning all three tiers, dev_config.py is the shared config module (6 dependents across the backend): it loads dev_config.toml, exposes the per-server auth-bypass flag for local testing, detects the IdP from token claims, and crucially strips spoofable keys like department from the X-Abac-Attrs header so clients cannot forge ABAC attributes. The accompanying templates document the environment variables, the group-to-role permission map, and the auth-bypass switches every service reads.

tour.title: Validating the Three-Tier Model
tour.description: Finally, the test suite proves the security model from Steps 4-9 actually holds. test_cedar_smoke.py runs the Cedar RBAC/ABAC policies in-process (including department-scoped ServiceNow and the protected/ guardrail), test_access_control.py exercises all three tiers against the live gateway, and test_abac_security.py is a regression guard ensuring the header parser from Step 10 cannot be tricked into accepting a spoofed department. The TESTING guide ties the suite together and explains the live-service and real-token modes.
